I now have a complete picture of the codebase. Here are the findings.

---

## Critical

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim/T1__leveraged__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:16`** — SQL injection via f-string query construction

What: `user_id` from `request.query` is interpolated directly into the SQL string with an f-string: `f"SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = '{user_id}'"`. Any caller-supplied value becomes raw SQL.

Why: An attacker can pass `id=' OR '1'='1` or similar payloads to bypass the WHERE clause, enumerate rows, or (on real engines) escalate to data destruction or exfiltration. This is a textbook, exploitable SQL injection.

Suggested direction: Replace the f-string with a parameterised query — pass the value as the second argument to `_DB.execute()` using `?` as the placeholder: `_DB.execute("SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE id = ?", (user_id,))`. The `validator.is_valid_id` helper already exists in the same repo and was clearly written for this purpose but is never called here; it should be called first to reject malformed IDs before the query even runs.

---

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim/T1__leveraged__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:14`** — unvalidated `None` query parameter crashes the route

What: `request.query.get("id")` returns `None` when the `id` key is absent. That `None` is then interpolated into the f-string as the literal string `"None"`, producing the query `WHERE id = 'None'`. If parameterised queries are adopted, sqlite3 will raise `InterfaceError` instead. Either way the endpoint silently misbehaves or crashes rather than returning a clean 400.

Why: Any unauthenticated-or-authenticated request without an `id` parameter hits this path. It is an unhandled input edge case that will surface as a 500 in production.

Suggested direction: After auth passes, check that `user_id` is not `None` (or equivalently call `is_valid_id`) and return a 400 response early. This should happen before any query is constructed.

---

## Important

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim/T1__leveraged__r1/work/service/routes/users.py:7-9`** — module-level mutable singleton database connection shared across all requests

What: `_DB` is a single `sqlite3.Connection` created at import time. `sqlite3` connections are not thread-safe by default (`check_same_thread=True`), so concurrent requests will raise `ProgrammingError`. Even in a single-threaded context, there is no isolation between requests.

Why: If the server is ever run with a threaded or async worker (which is the default for virtually every WSGI/ASGI server), this will produce intermittent, hard-to-reproduce crashes.

Suggested direction: Either pass `check_same_thread=False` and guard with a lock, or create a per-request connection. For a persistent store the conventional approach is a connection-per-request context manager; for tests, an in-memory DB fixture injected via dependency injection rather than a module global.

---

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim/T1__leveraged__r1/work/tests/test_users.py`** — no test coverage for missing/invalid `id` parameter or SQL-injection input

What: The test file covers only the happy path (known user, correct auth) and the no-auth gate. There are no tests for: absent `id`, unknown `id` (404 branch), or an `id` value that would be dangerous under the current implementation.

Why: The two branches that are broken right now (missing id, SQL injection) have zero test coverage, so the bugs will not be caught by the suite even after a fix is attempted.

Suggested direction: Add tests for `qid=None`, `qid` that matches no row (expect 404), and at least one structurally adversarial `qid` value (e.g. containing a single quote) to act as a regression guard.

---

## Nice to have

**`/C:/Users/filip/AppData/Local/Temp/leverage-bench-2026-05-23_v0.10.0-cold-post-trim/T1__leveraged__r1/work/service/validator.py:9`** — `is_valid_id` accepts a `str` type hint but guards against `None` internally

What: The function signature declares `value: str` but the first body line is `if value is None: return False`, implying callers may pass `None`. This type hint is misleading and the defensive check suggests the real contract is `Optional[str]`.

Why: Minor maintainability issue — the type hint and the runtime guard contradict each other, which can confuse static analysis tools (mypy will warn on call sites that pass `Optional[str]`).

Suggested direction: Change the signature to `value: str | None` (or `Optional[str]`) to match the actual accepted input, consistent with what `get_user` would pass after the missing-id fix.
